column1: # The values this mod patches, one per line:
#   FILE<TAB>PROPERTY<TAB>BASE<TAB>OP<TAB>LIMIT<TAB>SCOPE
# FILE is the MBIN path the game uses, relative to the data root.
# PROPERTY is the field to rewrite.
# BASE is the value the game ships today.
# OP is mul (BASE x factor) or div (BASE / factor).
# LIMIT is the upper bound for mul and the lower bound for div, so no value
# can reach zero or run away. The floor has to stay low enough that the
# manoeuvre can still be shortened by the same factor as the flight at the
# highest factor offered, or the ship arrives mid manoeuvre again.
# SCOPE tags the row. A variant asks for scopes with a factor each, so one
# group can be scaled differently from another.
# The render step turns this table into the Lua patch list and into the
# expected values that make verify checks the built EXML against.
# The scopes:
#   forces    the steering forces that push a ship toward a dock, and that
#             turn it into alignment on the way
#   approach  the speed of the flight along the approach to the pad
#   descent   the speed the ship drops onto the pad
#   bounce    the spring settle and the bounce when the ship touches down
#   manoeuvre the time the ship spends lining up with the pad
# What testing in game showed:
#   forces    raising them speeds up the turn into alignment, but the
#             flight to the pad stays a crawl
#   approach  raising it speeds up the flight to the pad, but the ship
#             arrives before it has finished turning
#   Both at the same factor, so the turn and the flight stay in step.
#   The ship still lands upside down at the higher factors. Neither more
#     force, nor a longer landing window, nor a longer tip manoeuvre
#     gives the ship the spin it needs: the alignment is a manoeuvre of
#     fixed length, and the flight has to be short enough that the
#     manoeuvre still fits inside it. At 2x it fits, at 10x the ship
#     arrives mid manoeuvre and lands upside down.
#   So the manoeuvre is shortened by the same factor as the flight.
# 10x is the ceiling. A 100x option was built and tested in game and the
# ship did not land right, so it is not offered.
# Deliberately left alone:
#   the descent speed, which shortens the same window
#   the tip length and the angle the ship may tip up to. Raising those
#     makes the ship fly on past the pad and over rotate, which is worse
#     than the problem it was meant to fix.
#   the roll the ship applies on its own and the roll during the docking
#     approach. Neither made the spin any faster.
# The outposts are not in this table. Their landing runs on different values
# and the outpost files are not patched, so a landing at an outpost is left
# as the game ships it.
# Ruled out by testing, and deliberately absent:
#   the cap on a ship's approach speed was in the first build, which
#     changed nothing
#   the player's own ship settings (the speed damper near a space base, the
#     approach speed cap when arriving from the anomaly, the cockpit
#     approach multiplier and the distance band the damper applies over)
#     were in the Minimal build, which also changed nothing. That layer
#     also governs how hard you can close on a station yourself, so leaving
#     it alone is the better outcome.
# The docking rotation speed is deliberately absent too. It lives in
# GCSPACESHIPGLOBALS and belongs to Faster Spaceship Docking Rotation
# Reloaded, and this mod must not fight it.
# The game's own spelling of LandingManuevreTime is missing a "u". Do not
# "fix" it here: the name has to match the data byte for byte, and make
# verify fails on a property that is not in the patch.
